events.blurb: Florence expels Dante and sentences him to burning if he returns. In exile he writes the Comedy, and the Black and White Guelph feud that cast him out becomes the poem's political spine.
events.label: Dante exiled, 1302

events.blurb: Henry VII of Luxembourg crosses the Alps to restore imperial authority in Italy, the last emperor to campaign seriously for the Italian crown. Dante hails him as a savior; the cities mostly resist.
events.label: Henry VII enters Italy, 1310

events.blurb: Henry VII dies of fever at Buonconvento while campaigning against Naples. His expedition collapses, and no emperor will rule Italy again.
events.label: Henry VII dies, 1313

events.blurb: Cosimo de' Medici returns from exile and becomes Florence's uncrowned ruler, ruling through the republic's institutions while funding Brunelleschi, Donatello, and Ficino.
events.label: Cosimo returns, 1434

events.blurb: Cosimo dies, honored as Pater Patriae, father of his country. His son Piero inherits the Medici bank, the family's political machine, and its debts.
events.label: Cosimo dies, 1464

events.blurb: Niccolò Machiavelli is born in Florence, the son of a lawyer, into a republic that has just passed from Cosimo's heirs to Lorenzo the Magnificent.
events.label: Machiavelli born, 1469

events.blurb: Lorenzo the Magnificent takes power in Florence at twenty, ruling as prince in all but name and bankrolling the artists and humanists who define the age.
events.label: Lorenzo takes power, 1469

events.blurb: Lorenzo dies at forty-three, and his son Piero proves unequal to the French invasion two years later. Florence expels the Medici and the republic returns.
events.label: Lorenzo dies, 1492

events.blurb: Rodrigo Borgia is elected Pope Alexander VI, and sets about carving a state in central Italy for his son Cesare, using the papacy as a family enterprise.
events.label: Alexander VI elected, 1492

events.blurb: After the Medici fall, the Dominican friar Girolamo Savonarola rules Florence as a moral dictator, burning vanities and preaching against the corrupt papacy.
events.label: Savonarola rises, 1494

events.blurb: Ludovico Sforza, who invited the French into Italy to secure his own claim, becomes Duke of Milan in name as well as fact.
events.label: Ludovico becomes duke, 1494

events.blurb: Savonarola is hanged and burned in the Piazza della Signoria, excommunicated and condemned after his theocracy collapses. Florence returns to republican government.
events.label: Savonarola executed, 1498

events.blurb: Machiavelli enters the Florentine chancery as secretary, beginning fourteen years of diplomatic missions to France, the papacy, and Cesare Borgia's camp, the education behind his political writing.
events.label: Machiavelli enters the chancery, 1498

events.blurb: The French capture Ludovico Sforza at Novara and carry him to France, where he dies in prison. Milan's independence ends with him.
events.label: Ludovico captured, 1500

events.blurb: Giuliano della Rovere is elected Pope Julius II, the warrior pope who will commission the Sistine Ceiling, raise the League of Cambrai, and personally lead armies in the field.
events.label: Julius II elected, 1503

events.blurb: Alexander VI dies, probably of malaria, and Cesare Borgia's state collapses within months. Machiavelli, who watched Cesare's rise, takes the lesson that fortune abandons even the ablest prince.
events.label: Cesare Borgia falls, 1503

events.blurb: When the Medici return with a Spanish army, Machiavelli is arrested, tortured on the strappado, and retired to his farm at Sant'Andrea. There he writes The Prince.
events.label: Machiavelli arrested, 1513

events.blurb: Giovanni de' Medici is elected Pope Leo X, Lorenzo's son, who will spend the papacy's fortune on art and war and face Luther's revolt four years later.
events.label: Leo X elected, 1513

events.blurb: Cardinal Giulio de' Medici commissions Machiavelli to write the Florentine Histories, the republic's official history from its origins to Lorenzo's death.
events.label: Machiavelli commissioned, 1520

events.blurb: Machiavelli dies at fifty-eight, days after the Sack of Rome and the last expulsion of the Medici, hoping in vain for a post in the restored republic.
events.label: Machiavelli dies, 1527

events.blurb: Charles V is crowned Holy Roman Emperor by the pope at Bologna, the last imperial coronation in Italy. The emperor who sacked Rome three years earlier now poses as the Church's protector.
events.label: Charles V crowned at Bologna, 1530

events.blurb: Catherine de' Medici, born in Florence and married into the French royal house, becomes Queen of France. She will rule through her sons for thirty years of religious war.
events.label: Catherine becomes queen, 1547

events.blurb: On St Bartholomew's Day, Parisian Catholics massacre thousands of Huguenots gathered for a royal wedding. Catherine's part in the decision remains debated; the massacre defines her reputation.
events.label: St Bartholomew's Day, 1572

events.blurb: Catherine de' Medici dies at Blois, having outlived her husband and three king sons. The Valois dynasty she held together dies with her son Henry III seven months later.
events.label: Catherine dies, 1589
